title: Visualize optimization portfolio decision distribution
description:
As an operator, I want stakeholder-safe visual explanations of optimization opportunity so that I can distinguish a steep priority drop-off, understand why a score ranks highly, and compare selected candidates with policy-deferred scores.

Scope: dashboard visualization and existing stakeholder presentation fields only; no new backend resource, GraphQL schema, or client-specific data.

Feature: Optimization opportunity evidence visualization

Scenario: Preserve evidence rank and policy disposition
Given evidence-ranked optimization opportunity rows
When an operator views the distribution component
Then it shows the complete pre-policy ranked curve with labeled selected, eligible, cooldown, blocked, and incomplete dispositions
And the operator can choose linear or logarithmic opportunity scale
And excluded rows remain visible and interactive.

Scenario: Explain the components of opportunity
Given a score with valid feedback volume and a disagreement rate
When the operator views its opportunity mark or text equivalent
Then the disagreement rate and feedback volume are visible alongside reviewed-error opportunity
And their units are explicit
And visual encoding does not rely on color alone.

Scenario: Protect stakeholder-safe output
Given portfolio presentation data
When the visualization renders
Then no opaque identifiers, raw feedback, prompts, transcripts, or reviewer comments are displayed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented a reusable client-side opportunity-distribution component and focused tests in the integration worktree. It renders every numerically valid evidence-ranked row as a curve, overlays distinct decision marks, includes a visible labeled legend and expandable text equivalent, and supports linear/logarithmic views with an explicit zero-value note. Validation passed: focused Jest suite (3 tests) and dashboard typecheck. No existing renderer, API/schema, or backend files were changed; no commit was created.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Acceptance update: the opportunity distribution now renders the complete evidence-ranked curve with distinct marks for selected, eligible, cooldown, blocked, and incomplete dispositions. Linear and logarithmic controls update in place, a full text equivalent remains available, and focused dashboard tests/typechecks passed. Visual DOM validation confirmed the curve and disposition marks render.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Follow-up scope: extend the existing opportunity-distribution component with stakeholder-safe visual encodings and text-equivalent columns for disagreement rate and valid feedback volume. The implementation remains dashboard-only and does not require backend schema changes. I will add a failing focused component specification before updating the component.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Completed the feedback-signal extension. The existing chart now accepts optional disagreement-rate and valid-feedback-count values without a backend contract change. Marker size uses normalized valid feedback volume; a visible inner fill uses normalized disagreement rate; both are explained in text and carried in the accessible table and tooltip. Missing/invalid values remain visibly unavailable in text and use the neutral marker baseline. Tests were written first and initially failed, then passed after implementation. Validation: focused Jest suite 4/4, dashboard web/backend typecheck, and targeted diff check. No commit was created.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Incremental implementation now adds two stakeholder-safe visual signals to every evidence-ranked point: marker size represents valid feedback volume and inner fill represents disagreement rate. Exact counts and percentages remain available in the tooltip and text-equivalent table. The stakeholder presentation reuses existing fields and adds no schema or backend resource. Focused frontend/backend tests and typechecks passed.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Production-backed read-only acceptance passed on commit eeb696a23. The living Report updated in place with 31 evidence-ranked rows; rendered marker radii varied from 1.2 to 10 pixels, demonstrating real volume and disagreement variation. The text equivalent reconciled opportunity, disagreement percentage, valid feedback count, disposition, and policy reason for all rows. The run used zero optimizer cost, zero semantic diagnoses, and made no score mutations. Report and embedded Procedure ended honestly as Incomplete.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Live visual inspection found that the new size and inner-fill calculations were present, but disposition colors rendered as black because the component wrapped already-complete CSS color variables in another color function. Follow-up acceptance will require valid disposition colors plus an explicit visual encoding key for low/high feedback volume and disagreement. I will first extend the focused component specification and confirm it fails before correcting production code.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Follow-up acceptance passed. The chart now uses valid existing dashboard color variables, its visual key shows low/high examples for feedback volume and disagreement, and disagreement fill is area-proportional so moderate rates remain legible. Focused component and report-status suites passed (5 tests), dashboard frontend/backend typechecks passed, diff check passed, and live browser inspection confirmed colored dispositions plus distinct marker size and inner-fill signals. No schema or backend resource changed.
